proposed_from.topic: Fix the three-variable cyclic SEM X1=aX2+eps1, X2=bX1+cX3+eps2, X3=dX2+eps3 with abcd nonzero and 1-ab-cd nonzero. Disturbances are centered, non-Gaussian, have finite third moments, satisfy eps1 independent of eps3 and the path connected-set Markov plus Tramontano-Drton-Etesami independence-genericity conditions; eps2 may depend arbitrarily on both outer disturbances. The information input is the observed cumulant tensor through order K in {2,3}; the query is only (a,d). For candidate (alpha,delta), define residual cross-cumulants F11, F21 and F12. Construct the explicit observed-cumulant chart D and prove that D nonzero makes their complex common zero set the singleton (a,d), with a rational inverse from the linear first subresultant of two observable cubics. On a nonempty covariance-regular locus, construct a smooth one-dimensional legal order-two fiber for (a,d), proving the least identifying order is three; also prove the full observed law retains a two-dimensional (b,c) fiber. Estimate (a,d) by feasible overidentified GMM on a compact sixth-Wasserstein regular subclass with quantitative chart, Jacobian and influence-covariance margins, and derive a uniformly valid sandwich ellipse. Explicitly distinguish Draisma-Kuhnt-Zwiernik, Jiang, Mesters-Zwiernik, Ribot-Seigal-Zwiernik and the banked general cumulant-transfer obstruction. Consumer: a prospective BayCausal/WIHS extension may report outer coefficients as robust under an independently justified overlapping-cycle/path-dependence motif while leaving central coefficients as a sensitivity fiber; do not claim its published disjoint-cycle theorem already covers this motif. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The residual covariance equation eliminates delta as t(alpha)/l(alpha); substituting into F21 and F12 gives two observable cubics P and Q. On the nonzero chart, their first subresultant is linear, yielding a=-s0/s1 and d=t(a)/l(a). Exact expansion verifies the legal exponential-source witness, all chart factors, the singleton residual ideal, a rank-two Jacobian, 100 fresh rational perturbations, and a nonlinear-middle stress case. A five-source construction realizes every nearby positive-definite path covariance with independent non-Gaussian endpoints, producing a one-dimensional order-two query fiber; an explicit residual shear preserves a two-dimensional full-law central-coefficient fiber. Literature checks found no query-specific cyclic order-three inverse. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniform asymptotic linearity of feasible optimally weighted GMM on the stated compact sixth-moment class, including centered third-cumulant influence functions, covariance estimation, separation, and margin diagnostics. EARLY KILL TEST: Implement the fixed cubic subresultant using only observed tensors with the true mechanism hidden; reproduce both witness families and exact covariance twins on a rational neighborhood. Stop if a nontrue common root survives with D nonzero, specialization fails, or the covariance realization leaves the legal model. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest identification paper is Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami, which gives a necessary-and-sufficient acyclic direct-effect criterion, only partial cyclic results, and a whole-distribution residual-transfer argument. The present kernel instead fixes an overlapping two-cycle motif and claims a finite-order, observable, rational recovery map for only the outer coefficients, together with a legal covariance fiber proving that order three is minimal on a nonempty regular locus. Mesters and Zwiernik are the closest cumulant-elimination and minimum-distance comparator, but their full-mixing results use standardized uncorrelated components and stronger global tensor-zero patterns; the middle-error mixed third cumulants allowed here invalidate that reduction. The precise new object is the observable chart \(D=v\chi p_3q_3s_1\), whose nonvanishing is claimed to make the complex residual fiber a singleton and whose linear first subresultant gives the inverse. The statistical open content is a uniform feasible-GMM expansion over a quantitatively regular sixth-Wasserstein class, not a claim that pointwise GMM theory is new. Chen and coauthors' latent-confounded higher-cumulant rank criterion is acyclic and therefore does not subsume either the cyclic residual-elimination inverse or its legal order-two lower-information fiber.

seed_details.title: A rational third-cumulant inverse for the outer coefficients of two overlapping feedback cycles
seed_details.anchor_opened: The introduction, Section 6, the error-transfer construction, Theorem 5.1, and the conclusion of Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami were read; the tensor-zero identification argument in Theorem 5.5 and the global-branch warning surrounding Proposition 5.17 of Mesters and Zwiernik were also read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The published cyclic argument is full-distribution and only partial; the first changed step is to replace support constraints on an unknown residual-transfer matrix by the three observable equations \(F_{11}=F_{21}=F_{12}=0\), eliminate \(\delta\), and certify the remaining common root with a fixed cubic subresultant.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for `cyclic SEM third cumulant subresultant outer coefficient', `overlapping two-cycle residual cumulant identification', and citations to Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami located no query-specific rational inverse.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami because their cyclic residual-transfer lemma already characterizes observationally equivalent coefficients.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their cyclic section supplies only partial full-law criteria and no finite-order observable polynomial map; the proposed singleton complex fiber and linear first-subresultant inverse are new target-specific claims.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed uses structure identification rather than an effect-identification default, names the chart \(D\), gives a computable inverse, and includes a necessity-side information lower bound in the combined kernel.

seed_details.title: A sharp order-two versus order-three information frontier for the outer query
seed_details.anchor_opened: The introduction, cyclic-model Lemma 9 and its covariance-fiber construction, and the conclusion of Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant were read, together with Section 6 and the conclusion of Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Covariance noninjectivity for a directed cycle does not imply a legal query-moving fiber under endpoint independence. The first changed step is to solve the outer residual covariance equation locally and realize every nearby path covariance by five independent non-Gaussian sources.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing `least cumulant order' with `cyclic structural equation model' and `outer coefficients' found covariance noninjectivity and full-mixing tensor recovery, but no sharp query-level order frontier.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant because any cyclic covariance map is already known to be noninjective.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their generic two-point fiber concerns a simple directed cycle with diagonal error covariance; it neither preserves the present path-dependent disturbance class nor proves that the projected fiber moves \((a,d)\).
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The lower bound is a smooth legal fiber on a strict regularity region, not a hand-tuned covariance twin or a failed-rank certificate.

seed_details.title: Uniform feasible optimal-weight inference for a chart-identified residual-cumulant query
seed_details.anchor_opened: The minimum-distance construction, consistency proposition, asymptotic-normality proposition, and conclusion of Mesters and Zwiernik were read; the estimation section and confidence-interval paragraph in the conclusion of Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to replace pointwise tensor minimum distance by a uniform expansion for parameter-dependent centered residual cumulants, with the optimal weight and its influence covariance estimated from the same sample.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for uniform cumulant GMM in cyclic structural models found Hansen's general GMM theory, Jiang's pointwise smooth-map limit, and weak-identification work for other models, but no uniform sixth-Wasserstein result for this residual score.
seed_details.red_team: Routine from Hansen and Mesters and Zwiernik because the moment vector is finite-dimensional and polynomial.
seed_details.rebuttal: Pointwise GMM does not supply uniform centering remainders, same-sample weight consistency, global separation, or coverage over a Wasserstein-compact class; these are the load-bearing open steps.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is a limit-law kernel with explicit regime margins, not a bare estimation rung or a rate claim driven by an oracle nuisance assumption.

seed_details.title: A distribution-preserving central-coefficient shear inside the path-dependent cyclic model
seed_details.anchor_opened: The residual-transfer representation in Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami and the model-equivalence construction and conclusion of Lacerda, Spirtes, Ramsey, and Hoyer were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to restrict the full-law transfer matrix to a middle-row shear that fixes the two outer normalized rows while preserving endpoint independence in both directions.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for a central-parameter orbit in overlapping cyclic LiNG models found only full-model equivalence classes and the general residual-transfer framework.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from the known graphical transformation group because the allowed path graph has a two-parameter lower-triangular stabilizer.
seed_details.rebuttal: The Gaussian concentration-model group does not itself prove preservation of the non-Gaussian independence-genericity condition; the two-sided residual argument is still needed, although this seed is better used as a companion result than as the headline.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed does not claim that the Gaussian group theorem is a cyclic non-Gaussian identification result.

seed_details.title: A semialgebraic atlas of real outer-query fibers on the exceptional chart
seed_details.anchor_opened: The polynomial zero-pattern reduction and branch discussion of Mesters and Zwiernik and the explicit cyclic covariance-fiber analysis of Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is a real, moment-feasible primary decomposition of \(\langle F_{11},F_{21},F_{12}\rangle\) after each factor of \(D\) vanishes, rather than a complex dimension count.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for real residual-cumulant fiber atlases found no treatment of this motif, but also no evidence that a compact closed-form stratification is feasible.
seed_details.red_team: The chart complement mixes harmless degree drops with genuine nonidentification, so a complete atlas is a large computer-algebra project rather than one theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: No adequate bounded rebuttal survived the scan.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed avoids equating \(D=0\) with nonidentification, but its scope is not yet controlled.

seed_details.title: Identification-robust confidence sets near a vanishing subresultant chart
seed_details.anchor_opened: The confidence-interval discussion of Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami and the introduction and weak-GMM continuity argument of Andrews and Mikusheva were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to derive the local experiment for two observable cubics approaching a nontransverse common root before importing test inversion or quasi-Bayes smoothing.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found subvector Anderson--Rubin theory for linear instrumental variables and weak-GMM continuity results, but no nonlinear subresultant analogue.
seed_details.red_team: Generic weak-GMM test inversion already gives coverage without using the subresultant geometry.
seed_details.rebuttal: Existing results do not give the required local experiment or a boundedness criterion for this nonlinear polynomial query, but that derivation is too speculative for the first version.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is not mislabeled as ordinary Wald inference; coverage would come from identification-robust inversion.

seed_details.title: Graph-constrained coordinate recovery below the pairwise mean-independence threshold
seed_details.anchor_opened: The introduction, Theorems 1.3--1.5, the maximality construction, and the discussion of Ribot, Seigal, and Zwiernik were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to intersect their nonidentifiable full-mixing orbit with the normalized SEM zero pattern and project the intersection onto selected rows.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining pairwise mean independence with graph-constrained coordinate recovery found acyclic residual algorithms but no cyclic query theorem.
seed_details.red_team: The fixed three-variable example cannot establish a general frontier below pairwise mean independence.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for a flagship claim; a graph-family theorem would be required.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The broad seed is not substituted for the defensible fixed-motif theorem.

seed_details.title: A third-order observable certificate for independence genericity in the fixed path motif
seed_details.anchor_opened: Theorem 5.1, its finite-cumulant genericity proof, its examples, and the relaxing-independence paragraph of the conclusion were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step would lower the anchor's generic finite-order certificate from at most \(2(p+1)\) to order three after imposing the fixed path and structural sparsity.
seed_details.destination_search: No exact third-order certificate was found, but the query inverse only needs the anchor condition maintained, not empirically certified.
seed_details.red_team: Theorem 5.1 already supplies finite-order genericity, and lowering its certificate for three nodes does not identify the maintained disturbance graph.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds as a standalone contribution.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The selected proposal keeps independence genericity as maintained structure and does not sell its empirical verification.

seed_details.title: An overidentification test for the residual path restriction after outer-query recovery
seed_details.anchor_opened: The minimum-distance testing discussion of Mesters and Zwiernik and the cumulant-estimator and Wald-test sections of Jiang were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to account for estimating \((a,d)\) when converting the third residual restriction into a one-degree-of-freedom specification statistic.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found generic GMM overidentification tests and Jiang's test of uncorrelated errors, but no test that validates the path motif itself.
seed_details.red_team: This is the standard Hansen overidentification statistic once the two parameters are estimated from three moments.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection largely holds; the centering and chart details are useful but not a standalone kernel.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The test is retained only as a possible corollary of the uniform GMM result.
